answer: An agent joins only by bonding scarce collateral in a public registry and producing signed, externally checkable work that established agents can challenge. If a verifier proves that identities coordinated to inflate votes or reuse evidence, the protocol burns their bonds and lowers their reputation. Calling the identities meadow, pearl, and comet changes nothing: every extra identity needs another deposit, while a fake quorum risks losing all collateral, making Sybil attacks costly.
